title: The release tier is green again: a large plan's report prints, and reach-diff runs on Windows
description: Follow-up to P152's CI run 41281241772. BUG-32: Chrome's printToPDF refuses the rendered report of this repository's own plan (about 10 MB). reach-diff, new in P152, never ran on Windows and fails its child-tracing cases there.
desiredOutcome: The live-plan browser leg passes on every runner at this repository's plan size with headroom measured, and tools/reach-diff.py's selftest passes on the windows cells, so ci/P152's head can land on main

findings.issue: rd92's argument tuple WINDOWS_ARGS only exercises two splitter branches at the END of the line: the empty argument is last (so the in-loop 'if started' separator test is never what keeps it) and the final backslash run is followed by a closing quote (the post-loop 'word.append(slash * run)' is never reached with run>0). Read by mutation in a scratch mirror: replacing the in-loop 'if started:' with 'if word:' (drops a mid-line empty argument) and deleting the post-loop backslash append (drops a trailing backslash on an unquoted last argument, e.g. a directory path ending in a backslash) both leave 162/162 green. Both are exactly the cases the task's brief named (empty arg, trailing backslashes). The splitter itself is correct for both (round-trip probe below), so this is a test gap, not a code bug.
findings.resolution: Add to WINDOWS_ARGS (or a third line in _windows_event_cases) an empty argument in the middle and an unquoted last argument ending in a backslash, e.g. ('exit-hard', '', 'D:\\out\\') ending after a non-empty arg, then re-run mutants 'if word:' and no post-loop append to see rd92 red.

tasks.title: reach-diff traces module children on Windows as it does on posix
tasks.description: On CI run 41281241772 both windows selftest cells fail tools/reach-diff.py: rd18, rd22, rd29, rd30, rd41, rd47, rd48 (untraced module children counted 0 at both sides) and rd62 (the 'untraced' refusal unasserted, a consequence). The failing log is saved in the orchestrator scratchpad (ci-P152-failed.log). Find why a child started on the module is not recognised on Windows (path separators or drive letters in the spawned-child key, the usercustomize/sitecustomize hook not loading, os.environ case, .start/.json files) and fix it so the same cases pass on windows; a posix-only assumption must become portable rather than skipped.

outcome.technical: Root cause, read from CPython's own source (subprocess.py, Python 3.14.7 here; 3.8 has the same branch): the Windows _execute_child joins args with list2cmdline (line 1477) BEFORE sys.audit('subprocess.Popen', executable, args, cwd, env) (line 1549), while the posix branch audits a list (lines 1845, 1858). The hook's on_event did module_at(args[1]), which returned -1 for anything not a list, so on Windows no traced process ever recorded a spawned module child, and untraced_children() was always empty. The log shows exactly that: start markers work ('4 processes started the hook and 3 wrote' in hard-exit), and recheck-processes named '<module> exit-hard' from the start markers, while every side printed '0 module children untraced'. Fix (tools/reach-diff.py only): a top-level _reach_diff_argv(args) in HOOK_SOURCE returns a list unchanged and splits a string back by the C runtime's rules (backslash runs before a quote, quote toggling, space/tab outside quotes). on_event uses it, and module_at takes its result. The comment above HOOK_SOURCE and the contract docstring now say what the hook does on Windows. New cases rd92/rd93 (in _windows_event_cases, called from _hook_cases) run the real hook in a child process that fires a Windows-shaped Popen audit event. A round-trip probe found 0 mismatches over 20000 random lists of a/B/:/\/"/space/tab/C// (seed 7). Each failure explained: rd18 (stripped env: the parent's spawned key was never recorded), rd22/rd29/rd30/rd41/rd47/rd48 (the hard-exit child started the hook but its parent never recorded it, so 0 untraced, no blind spot and no untraced refusal), and rd62 (no case produced the 'untraced' refusal, a consequence). o1 and x3 in the log are fixtures failing on purpose, printed inside passing cases. Not explained from the log, and not testable here: none of the failures is left unexplained. The path steps (normcase/realpath, the <tree>/<temp> mapping, the os.sep joins) already held on Windows, since start markers there carried module=True and '<module> exit-hard' keys. I could not run them under ntpath semantics, because ident/module_at are closures over os.path, so that part rests on the log, not on a case. Gates: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/reach-diff.py` exited 0, 162 cases (160 before). ruff check exited 0. vermin -t=3.8- over the file and the dumped hook text exited 0, minimum 3.8. Dependants: CONTRIBUTING.md still correct (it names the path, which is unchanged). hook_line, rebound, parse_args and settle are not touched, so tests/test__refs.py and the other name users are unaffected.
outcome.descriptive: reach-diff's hook now records module children on Windows, where Popen audits a joined command line instead of a list; that one cause explains all eight failing windows cases

verifiedBy: rd92: a hooked process fires subprocess.Popen's audit event with a list2cmdline-joined command line naming the module and Windows-shaped arguments (drive letters, mixed case, spaces, an embedded quote, trailing backslashes, an empty argument); the child is recorded with exactly those arguments and counted untraced
rd93: the over-fire direction - a command line holding the module's path only inside one quoted argument counts no module child

redFirst.basis: None owed: the task's mode is regression with tests.expectRedFirst false, and the new cases live in tools/reach-diff.py itself, so the helper's HEAD-plus-test-files tree would hold the fix as well. Observed by hand, not by the helper: before the fix existed, rd92 failed against the unfixed hook through a scratch driver of _hook_cases (2/3, traces['untraced'] == {}, the same {} the windows log prints). After the fix, on a scratch mirror: mutant 'never' (on_event takes args[1] only when it is a list) turned rd92 red (2/3); mutant 'always' (quotes dropped, split at every space) turned rd93 and rd92 red (1/3); the restored copy was byte-identical (cmp) and 3/3. __pycache__ was purged before every run, and the shared tree was never mutated.
